findings.problem: Driven at 390x844 the morning screen holds 206 characters and exactly one control, and that control opens backwards. Measured: .b-field is 715px on the day against 1674px in the received artifact; querying every interactive node on the day returns one, the "How you got here" summary, whose disclosure reveals the nine months that are already over. The measure — the object the whole direction is built on, seven rows of it in state=phone — is gone entirely on the one day it is about. A guest who opens the link at 07:00 and again at 16:00 gets a byte-identical screen: "Today", the date, "This is the day the plan was for", "Happening now: Wedding day at The Orchard", and a door to the past. Nothing says what is next, nothing moves, nothing pressable leads forward. Every other guest state gives the reader something to travel down; the flagship state gives them a poster and a back button.
findings.fix: Keep the artifact's structure on the day and change only what the day changes. Above the rule: "Today" stays exactly as it is, at the count's display step in the reading face. Below the rule, replace the single .b-sub sentence with the day's own running order — render the moments dated to the day itself as .b-item rows in the same list the artifact already uses, in order, each carrying its name and its place, and where a moment carries a time, that time in the count's slot in the mono face instead of a day count (the fixture already stacks two moments on one day, so the ordering and grouping machinery exists). Mark exactly one row data-now="true", drawn at full ink with the indigo tick, and set .b-measureHead to "now" rather than "days away"; every row after it stays at .b-title ink, every row before it drops to --fore-62, with no disclosure and no control on either, matching the record room's rule that the past is listed rather than folded. Leave "How you got here · 9 moments" where it is, below that block, for the months before. If a day carries only one moment, that one row is the running order and the screen still reads as a plan rather than a poster.

findings.problem: There is not one ":active" rule in master.html — grepped, zero matches against eight ":hover" rules. Driven at 1440 I put the mouse down on a row and held it: .b-grab's paint is identical between hover and pressed (background rgba(255,255,255,0.06) in both, colour rgb(255,255,255) in both, no transform, no border change). The hover model is otherwise good — .b-copy takes a 4% wash with a 12px halo — but hover is a desktop-only sense. On the phone, which is where the owner will actually add a moment while doing something else, the row's 544x83 hit area gives no feedback at all between the finger going down and the sheet arriving; the first thing that answers is the sheet itself. Surfaces at this bar answer the finger before they answer the intent.
findings.fix: Add a pressed step to the three control families, on the declared ladder at 0.08s with the one easing, ink only. .b-grab:active and .b-item:active .b-copy: background --fore-10 (up from --fore-06 / --fore-04) and no halo, so the press reads as the row settling. .b-act:active: background --fore-10; .b-act[data-primary="true"]:active: background --fore-72 (down from --fore-90). .b-step:active and .b-behindSummary:active: background --fore-10. Zero the transitions under prefers-reduced-motion with the existing block — the colour step itself stays, since it is state, not motion.

findings.element: state=ended — h1.b-who and the page's tab order
findings.problem: The h1 on the ended page is "Signal Timeline" — the wordmark. The news, "This link has been turned off.", is a p.b-endedTitle, and the project name "Mara & Finn" appears only inside a body paragraph. Every other guest state gives the h1 to the project (state=phone and state=day both read H1: "Mara & Finn"), so the single state a guest reaches when something has gone wrong is the only one whose heading tells them neither what happened nor which plan it happened to. Driven at 390 the page also returns zero focusable elements, so a keyboard or switch user lands on a document with nothing to land on and heading navigation delivers the brand name. A guest holding three shared links in the same thread cannot tell from the heading which one died.
findings.fix: Swap the two: set the h1 to "This link has been turned off" at the .b-endedTitle step, and demote "Signal Timeline" to the p.b-who kicker above it, exactly as .b-who sits above the count in state=phone. Put the project into the heading region — render the kicker as "Mara & Finn · Signal Timeline" so the first thing announced names the plan. Then give the page one place to land: make the owner's name a mailto link inside the sentence that already names them ("Orla can send a new link whenever they want to", with "Orla" the link) when the plan carries an owner contact; where there is no contact leave the sentence inert as it is now, but add tabindex="-1" and focus the h1 on load so the announcement is guaranteed rather than left to the reader to hunt for.

findings.element: state=loading — section.b-field[aria-busy] and its four .b-skel blocks
findings.problem: The frame's four bars match the arriving header to the pixel — 17 / 83 / 26 / 23 against .b-who 17, .b-num 86, .b-when 26, .b-sub 23 — and then it stops. Measured at 390: .b-field is 350px in state=loading and 1674px in state=phone, so the document grows from 900px to 1674px at the moment content lands and everything below the fourth bar arrives with no placeholder at all. At 1440 the frame also sits 26px higher than the artifact (.b-field top 68 vs 94), because the loading card is vertically centred by the [data-state="loading"] justify-content rule while the artifact is not, so the header the frame drew so carefully slides down 26px the instant it becomes real. The frame is right to invent no measure; it is wrong to also promise a card a fifth of the artifact's length.
findings.fix: Two changes, neither of which draws a tick or a count. First, drop "loading" from the justify-content: safe center rule (master.html line 204-207) so the loading field anchors on the same top edge the artifact uses; that removes the 26px slide. Second, after the "Today is 16 July" rule, reserve the measure's block: one empty div with min-height set to the artifact's measure height at that width (the same value the measure computes from the furthest count) carrying no children, no ticks, no bars and no border — then move "Bringing in what is ahead." to the top of that reserved block so the sentence sits where the first row will be rather than where the card currently ends. The page then arrives at its final length and nothing under the reader's thumb moves.

findings.element: state=day — summary.b-behindSummary and its details block
findings.problem: Driven at 390x844: pressing the summary grows the document from 844px to 1090px, leaves scrollY at 0, and leaves focus on the summary. The revealed rows run to a bottom of 950px, so the last two of the nine moments sit 106px below the fold with the page unscrolled and no cue that the list continues. The reader asked for the past and was handed a list whose end is off-screen; the paid-for lesson is that a change must play inside the visible area. It is the only reveal on the whole guest surface, so it is also the only chance the day has to show that pressing something does anything.
findings.fix: On the summary's toggle event, when it opens and the revealed block's bottom exceeds the viewport, scroll the block so its first row sits immediately under the summary (scrollIntoView with block "start" against the summary's bottom edge, on the 0.22s step and set to "auto" under prefers-reduced-motion), and leave focus on the summary where it already correctly stays. This is motion the reader asked for, on the declared ladder.

biggestWin: The owner's row is one object three ways at once. The pointer target is the whole 544x83 row (.b-grab::after, inset 0 — proved by driving it: the button intercepts a hover aimed at the title), the visible mark is a small underlined "Edit" chip present at rest rather than revealed on hover, and the accessible name is "Edit Menu tasting at The Orchard. Saturday 1 August, in 16 days. Shown to guests." — title, weekday, date, distance and visibility in one string. Hovering anywhere on the row washes the copy at 4% with a 12px halo and lifts the chip to full ink, and focus-within paints the identical state, so keyboard and pointer see the same surface. That is the hardest part of a dense editable list and it is solved: nothing hides until you point at it, nothing moves when you do, and the thing you press, the thing you see and the thing you hear are the same thing.
